note.question: How do repeated customer interactions affect assortment optimization for the multinomial logit model?
note.overview: This paper presents the multinomial logit model with repeated customer interactions. In each period, the same customer selects a product from the recommended assortment or opts out. From the seller’s perspective, the choice probability in the current period is updated based on the purchase history of the customer.

components.formal: Decision rule: Considers a seller offering assortments over time to an individual customer.
conditions: As in the classic MNL model, a customer has utility Un for product n ∈N , where Un ~ Gumbel(μn,1) is an independent (across customers and products) Gumbel random variable with mean μn and scale 1.
Note that the available products may or may not be the same across periods, and we allow for N i ∩N j ≠∅for i ≠j.
In each period, upon observing the offered assortment, the customer may purchase at most one product.
We include S[m] in the event for generality because the seller may choose to offer assortments adaptively and randomly in each period depending on the purchase history.
